limits: Draws a window, not the alignment; the identity it reports is the window's.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Draws an alignment someone else computed; the shading and conservation line are read from it, not inferred.
bio.jane/contract.question: What does this window of an alignment look like as a figure?

description: Draw a block of an alignment as an SVG figure: the rows named, the residues shaded by how much of their column agrees with them, the column numbers over the block and Easel's Clustal conservation line under it. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences. Name the window around whatever you are asking about — a variable site, a motif, a gap — because a 2,000-column alignment drawn at once shows nothing.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cell_width.description: width of one column's cell. In px. Advanced.

columns.description: how many columns to draw. Past about 200 the letters are narrower than the strokes that make them.

conservation.description: print the conservation line under the block.

from.description: first column drawn, 1-based and inclusive. Clamped into the alignment.

name_chars.description: how many characters of a row's name to print; a longer one is elided in the middle, keeping the tail where two rows of a family differ. Advanced.

row_height.description: height of one row. In px. Advanced.

rows.description: the ALIGNED rows, each {name, aligned}; every row must already be the same length. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences.

ruler.description: print the column numbers over the block. Advanced.

scheme.description: identity shades a residue by how much of its column agrees with it, which works for any alphabet; nucleotide paints QUEEN's own base colours and is IGNORED over protein rows, which the answer's `scheme` then says. Values: identity (Column identity), nucleotide (Base colours).

name: draw_alignment

alphabet.description: the alphabet the conservation line was computed for — Easel marks the strong and weak groups for protein only

columns.description: columns in the WHOLE alignment, so the window can be read against it

conservedColumns.description: columns in the window every row agrees on and none gaps — the `*` marks

firstColumn.description: first column drawn, 1-based inclusive, AFTER clamping

meanIdentity.description: mean per-column identity over the window drawn, 0-1 — the window's, not the alignment's

scheme.description: the scheme ACTUALLY used, which is `identity` whenever `nucleotide` was asked for over protein rows

svg.description: the alignment block as an SVG figure
